title: Quantinuum Demonstrates 99.9995% Logical Memory Fidelity on Helios Trapped-Ion Processor - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Quantinuum reports a logical memory fidelity of 99.9995% on its Helios trapped-ion computer using distance-7 triangular color codes, with a measured error-suppression factor of 12 per distance step. It ties the results to its 2029 Apollo fault-tolerant system target.

insights.claim: Quantinuum measured a logical error rate of 5 x 10^-6 per syndrome-extraction round on a distance-7 triangular color code on Helios, equal to 99.9995% logical memory fidelity.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A reported logical error rate in the 10^-6 range per round is a notable benchmark for trapped-ion QEC, though it is company-reported.
insights.quote: a logical memory fidelity of 99.9995%—equivalent to a logical error rate of 5 × 10-6 per syndrome-extraction round on a distance-7 code

insights.claim: Logical error per cycle fell from 5.5e-4 at distance 3 to 3.8e-5 at distance 5 and 5.0e-6 at distance 7, which Quantinuum describes as exponential suppression with a factor of 12 per distance step, or 144x from d=3 to d=7.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Operating well below threshold with constant suppression is the core evidence that scaling the code distance keeps paying off.
insights.quote: Each step increase in code distance suppressed logical memory errors by a factor of 12.

insights.claim: Quantinuum projects that logical error rates of 10^-12 across 100 logical qubits can be reached with about 30,000 physical qubits at the measured suppression factor, fewer than lower-suppression regimes would need.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Higher suppression factors directly reduce the physical-qubit count and cost of useful fault-tolerant machines.
insights.quote: Quantinuum projects that target logical error rates of 10-12 across 100 logical qubits can be achieved with ~30,000 physical qubits

insights.claim: A two-block transversal CNOT between distance-5 codes had a logical error of 7.0e-5 per gate, with a logical Clifford suppression factor of 9.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Logical gates, not just memory, are showing sub-threshold scaling, which is needed for computation.

insights.claim: Helios combines hardware 1762 nm optical repumping over 3 cycles, which cut leakage 6.5x, with software SWAP-superdense leakage reduction circuits that cycle data and ancilla qubits through ion transport.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Leakage control at two layers is part of what enables the clean distance scaling.

insights.claim: Neural decoders (3D CNNs and round-token transformers) trained on emulator data ran on physical hardware without fine-tuning at 0.2 to 0.5 ms per round on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, suggesting real-time streaming decoding is feasible.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: GPU-based neural decoding ties quantum error correction to NVIDIA's compute stack and removes a feared real-time bottleneck.
insights.quote: Both neural models achieved per-round latencies between 0.2 ms and 0.5 ms on NVIDIA H100 hardware

insights.claim: The results are presented as consistent with performance targets for Apollo, Quantinuum's planned universal fault-tolerant quantum system targeted for 2029.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Helios data is being used to support the credibility of the 2029 fault-tolerance roadmap.
insights.quote: The empirical results align with the performance targets established for Apollo
